newsitem.title: USA: Former Media Vision VP agrees guilty plea to fraud.
newsitem.headline: Former Media Vision VP agrees guilty plea to fraud.

text.p: The former head of sales at now-defunct Media Vision Technology Inc. has agreed to plead guilty to wire fraud stemming from fraudulent reporting of the company's 1993 financial results, officials said Thursday.

Michael Humphress, formerly senior vice president of worldwide sales at Media Vision Technology, also settled a separate civil action filed by the Securities and Exchange Commission, the U.S. Attorney for northern California and the SEC said in a joint statement.

As part of the settlements of the criminal and civil actions, Humphress agreed to cooperate with authorities in their continuing investigations into securities fraud by senior management at Media Vision in 1993 and 1994, the statement said.

"The commission will continue to take aggressive action against high-level executives of Silicon Valley companies who commit financial fraud," David Bayless, the SEC's district administrator in San Francisco, said.

Fremont, Calif.-based Media Vision Technology assembled and sold multimedia computer upgrade kits, software and other computer products. The company, whose shares had been publicly traded on Nasdaq, sought Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in July 1994.

In December 1994, the stockholders' equity interests were rendered worthless by the bankruptcy court, when it confirmed a plan of reorganization. In May 1996, the company changed its name to Aureal Semiconductor Inc.

Under a plea agreement with federal prosecutors, Humphress agreed to plead guilty to one count of wire fraud, the federal officials said. The charge carries a potential prison sentence of five years, a $250,000 fine and restitution to victims of the fraud, they said.

The SEC alleged that Humphress authorised shipment of unordered product to inflate revenues, avoided recognition of product returns and falsely told auditors that amounts listed in company documents as owed by customers could be collected.

Without admitting or denying the SEC allegations, Humphress agreed to a final judgment ordering him to pay $200,000 in civil penalties and barring him from serving as an officer or director of any public company, the federal officials said.
Douglas Young, an attorney for Humphress, said his client was a responsible individual.

"In this situation, it's his effort to be responsible and to act with integrity by working with the ongoing government investigations to see that the events that are of concern to the government can and will be resolved in the appropriate way," Young said.

The SEC complaint alleged Humphress violated federal securities laws by "substantially assisting Media Vision Technology Inc. in the fraudulent overstatement of its financial results for the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 1993."
It said executives at Media Vision began engaging in financial fraud by the third quarter of 1993.

In February 1994, Media Vision reported revenue for the 1993 fiscal year of $241.1 million and income of $19.9 million. The overstated financial statements led the market to overvalue Media Vision's stock, which collapsed from a high of $46.50 in January 1994 to $4.875 on May 5, 1994, it said.
In August 1994, the company restated its results for 1993, reporting revenue of $149.7 million and a loss of $99.2 million, the SEC said. Humphress was terminated by the company in May 1994.
